title: Rust tunnel_auth check_time rollback wipes replay/revocation floors; Python retains them (P-R divergence)
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-0rep (two reviewers converged, P1). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:419-425 check_time() calls self.clear() on clock rollback, wiping entries AND replay_floors and resetting last_now=None (clear():213-218). Python mirror python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py:405-414 _observe_time() clears ONLY _entries and explicitly retains floors/_revoked/_last_now with comment: 'Retain replay/revocation floors and the high-water time so a captured grant cannot rearm merely because the clock moved back'. Attack: attacker with a captured valid root-signed POST + ability to roll the gateway clock back replays it after rollback; Rust has no floors (wiped) and last_now=None so the backdated now passes check_time and expiry (claim.expiry<=backdated now), the post is re-accepted and re-arms the data plane; Python denies. Cross-impl divergence: same inputs, Rust accepts, Python denies. Also untested for floor retention (rollback test at :1009-1016 asserts denial only). Fix: mirror Python - clear() only entries on rollback (keep floors and last_now high-water), and pin with a unit test asserting floor retention post-rollback. Note: pinning test direction_scope_clock_and_capacity_fail_closed (:1009-1016) asserts UnauthorizedTunnel AFTER rollback because entries were wiped; with floors retained, authorize_decapsulation still denies (no entry) but the assertion reason may change - update per new semantics, do not weaken.
